Criminal Revision Nos. 739 of 1973, 3/74

full_judgment:
A.T.M. Masud, J.—These 20 appellants have been convicted under Article 2(4)(a)(i)(d) of the Bangladesh Schedule Offences (Special Tribunals) Order P.O. 50/72 and sentenced to R.I. for 3 years each and also to pay a fine of Taka 500/- each in default to further R.I. for 6 months each on 15-11-73 by Mr. M.A. Hye, Magistrate, 1st Class and Special Magistrate, Naogaon in G.R. Case No. 670/73. Criminal Appeal No. 739 of 1 973 has been preferred by appellants Sadeque Ali alias Sadequl Islam, Shamsuddin, Abdur Razzaque, Osman Ali Mondal, Mozahar alias Mozahar Ali. Criminal Appeal No. 3/74 has been preferred by Kazi Ansarul Islam and Alam Miah, Criminal Appeal No. 47/74 has been preferred by appellant Mosiruddin Akan alias Karai, Asiruddin Mondal and Jahurul Islam; Criminal Appeal No, 54/74 has been preferred by Muzaffar Hossain alias Choin; Criminal Appeal No. 66/74 has been preferred by appellant Abdul Latif; Criminal Appeal No. 104/74 has been preferred by appellants Abdur Rahim alias Jinnah, Abdul Majid, Malequl Islam and Azizul Islam alias Azizul Hoq and appeal No. 419/74 has been preferred by appellants Abdul Majid, Jafar Ali and Md. Matiar Rahman. The said Abdul Majid has subsequently filed an appeal through a lawyer in this Court along with other appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 104 of 1974. 

 P.W. 1 Badiruddin lodged the First Information Report with the Officer-in-Charge of Patnitala P.S. The Police started a case and after completing investigation submitted charge sheet against the appellants and one Tayab Ali (since acquitted) on 15-11-73 under sections 147/149/448/380 B.P.C. read with P,O. 50/72. 

 The Sub-divisional Magistrate, Naogaon after taking cognizance of the case transferred it to the Court of Mr. M.A. Hye, Magistrate 1st Class and Special Magistrate, Naogaon who hearing the witnesses convicted and sentenced the appellants as above by his judgment and order dated 15-11-73 in G.R. Case No. 670/73. In this case the prosecution examined 10 witnesses. The defence did not examine any witness. 

 3. P.W. 1 Badiruddin of mouja Aminabad, P.S. Patnitala has lodged F.1 R. in this case He has stated that on 28th Aswin, 1380 BS at about 12-00/1.00 A.M. about 400/ 500 miscreants holding a procession and shouting slogans entered into his house and forcibly took away his S.B.B.L. gun bearing Na. 78011. The miscreants were armed with rifles, S.L.R. and torch lights. He further stated that on the following day the miscreants also looted away guns of some other persons of different villages. The miscreants threatened him at the time of departure. He could not identify any accused person. In cross-examination he stated that he did not come out of his room on the night of occurrence. 

 4. P.W. 2 Majibar Rahman is a man of mouza P.S. Patnitala. He stated that on the night following 28th Aswin, 1380 B.S. he heard slogans and found 400/500 miscreants entered into his house with torch light and were armed with guns, rifles etc. They forcibly took awry his S.B B L. gun bearing No. 102487 and 10/12 cartridges. He identified the appellants in dock and stated that they were members of the procession. He stated that subsequently the police recovered his stolen gun. In cross-examination he stated that there was a burning hurricane in his dwelling hut at the time of occurrence. He admitted that he could not identify accused Razzaque and Osman by name. 

 5. P.W. 3 Abdul Gafur is a man of village and mouja Aminabad P.S. Patnitala. He has stated that on the night following 28th Aswin 1380 B.S. at about 12-30 A.M. about 400/4300 miscreants being armed with rifles etc. shouting slogan entered into his house and forcibly took away his S B.B.L. gun bearing No. 7416 with 30 cartridges. They also fired-six rounds towards his house. He stated that accused Azizul Islam, Majid and others (identified in dock) entered into his house and he could recognise them at the focus of their torch light. They also assaulted his father in cross-examination he stated that the accused persons focused torch lights at a distance of 6/7 cubits from his room and that he was in the upper stair of his house at the time of occurrence. He denied the defence suggestion that he was deposing falsely. 

 6. The learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the respective appellants in the aforesaid appeals have assailed the order of conviction and sentence on several grounds both on facts and law. It is contended by the learned Advocates of the appellant that different offences committed by different Occasions have been jointly tried in the present case and as such the joint trial of all the appellants in one trial has rendered the entire trial invalid. We find no substance in this contention. From the prosecute case as given out by the witnesses and as are found in the accusation of the appellants in their examination under Section 242 of the code of Criminal Procedure it would appear that the alleged offences have been committed by the accused persons in course of the same transaction and joint trial of such persons have been made permissible under section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 7. It was next argued that there was no proper compliance with the provisions of sections 242 and 342 Cr.P.C. in this case and the accused have been seriously prejudiced thereby. The trial was held in summary way. All the witnesses were examined and cross-examined on the same date. As soon as the accused appeared before the Court they were examined under section 242 Cr.P.C. and after the evidence was closed they were examined under section 342 Cr. P.C. The accused having no difficulty to understand the prosecution case against them in the facts and circumstances of the case, we find that there has been proper compliance with the provisions of sections 242 and 342 Cr.P.C. and the accused have in no way been prejudiced. No instance of such prejudice have been pointed out. 

 It is next contended that the prosecution has not been able to establish its case against the appellants beyond reasonable doubt by any reliable local witness. It is, therefore, necessary now to examine the cases of the individual appellants. 

 8. On an analysis of the evidence it appears that the appellants of all these appeals may be divided into 3 categories. In the first category would come the case of 4 appellants who were arrested along with arms and ammunitions and in the second category would come the case of 3 appellants who have been specifically named by the witnesses alleging that they participated in the procession being armed with rifles etc. and shouting slogans and in the 3rd category comes the cases of the appellants who have not been specifically named by any of the witnesses but simply have been identified in the dock. 

 10. Dr. Aleem-al-Razee, learned Advocate appearing for 3 of the appellants of this category, namely, Abdul Majid, Abdur Rahim and Malequl Islam of this category submitted that clients could not engage any defence lawyer at the trial and they did not get sufficient time for the purpose and as such they could not cross-examine the witnesses who deposed against them. On perusal of the records it, however, appeals that these accused were arrested on 31-10-73 and the trial was held on 15-11-73. So it cannot be said that they were not given sufficient lime or opportunity to engage lawyer to defend them. No application has also been filed on their behalf praying for adjournment of the trial to enable them to engage a lawyer. Dr. Razee has next contended that no seizure list has been proved in this case to show from whose possession the incriminating arms and ammunitions were recovered. It is true that no seizure list has been proved in the case but it is in evidence of P.Ws. 4 and 5 who arrested the 4 appellants along with arms and ammunitions from the house of P.Ws. 8 where they took shelter and they have produced the arrested appellants with arms and ammunitions before the Investigating Officer P.W. 10. All seized arms have been produced before the Court by the Investigating Officer P.W. 10 and marked Exts. II-V. In the circumstances the failure of the prosecution to prove the seizure list of the said arms and ammunitions do not in any way affect the prosecution case in respect of which there is overwhelming direct evidence. 

 11. Appellant Jafar Ali although of this category was not represented before us by any lawyer but we ourselves have examined the evidence adduced against him and we find his case to be on the same footing as that of the other 3 appellants represented by Dr. Razee. Considering the entire evidence End facts and circumstances of the case we are of the opinion that the guilt of these 4 appellants of this category namely, Abdul Majid, Malequl Islam, Abdur Rahim alias Jinnah and Jafar has been well established. 

 13. On an analysis of the evidence it appears that there is direct evidence against Azizul Islam and Abdul Majid. This Majid was also arrested along with arms and his case has been considered while discussing the case of the appellant of the first category. The evidence against accused Jahurul Islam is only of general nature. Only P.W. 4 has stated his name. No specific instance of his commission of any offence has been cited. In the circumstances, we think that the evidence against Jahurul Islam is not at all sufficient to establish his guilt. We, however, think that the guilt of appellant Azizul Islam and Abdul Majid has been well established. Appellant Abdul Majid has also been found guilty along with the appellants of the first category. 

 14. Now we will consider the case of the appellants of the 3rd category which includes the appellants Sadeque Ali, Shamsuddin, Abdur Razzaque, Osman Ali Mondal, Mozahar alias Mozahar Ali, Muzaffar Hussain alias Choin, Kazi Ansarul Islam, Alam Miah, Mosiruddin Akonda alias Kerai, Aziruddin Mondal, Matiur Rahman, Barju Pahan and Jenka Pahan. 

 15. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants of this category have vehemently argued that the general evidence led against them and the identification in lump in dock cannot be relied upon to establish the guilt of the appellants. It has been further argued that the appellants as well as the witnesses who have identified the appellants in dock are from different villages and under different police stations, and there being no evidence that the witnesses had previous acquaintances with the appellants and the witnesses not having been put on identification test no reliance should be placed on the said identification on dock by the witnesses. In this connection it has further been argued that the evidence was recorded under general terms to the effect that 400/500 miscreants entered into the houses of the witnesses and participated in procession raising slogans and the learned Magistrate simply recorded that the appellants were identified on dock without mentioning if the identification was by name or by place and this kind of omnibus evidence by itself cannot establish the guilt of the appellants. It was further argued that many charge sheet witnesses of the locality have not been examined and no explanation has been given for their non-examination. It was further pointed out that in the First Information Report lodged by P.W. 1 in whose house also the miscreants entered and looted his gun, not a single name of the miscreants has been mentioned. There is even no mention that he recognised any appellant in the trial Court also. P.W. 1 did not identify any appellant. Mr. Serajul Huq, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant Muzaffer Hossain alias Choin one of the appellants of this category has further argued that P.W. 4 has admitted in cross-examination that he did not see Choin taking part in any activity against the State. P.W. 5 also stated like that. P.W. 6 stated that appellant Choin alias Mujaffar was not present at his house at the time of occurrence. 

 16. Mr. Md. Ansar Ali, learned Advocate appearing for some of the appellants of this category has cited some decisions before us in support of his contention that the general evidence led against the appellants and the identification in dock should not be relied upon. In the case of Man Singh and others Vs Emperor, reported in A. I. R. 1929 (Allahabad) 928, it has been held that the evidence as to identification ought in each case to be subjected to a close and careful scrutiny. It is an important factor whether all the persons identified were previously known to the witnesses or were perfectly strangers to them. The time of occurrence, the state of light and the opportunities which the witnesses had of identifying are material circumstances. The range and distance from which the witnesses say that they saw the accused should be determined. 

 17. In the case of Beladin and others vs State of Uttar Pradesh reported in A. I. R. 1956 (SC)-181, the evidence was recorded in that case in general terms to the effect that all the appellants and many more were miscreants and were armed with deadly weapons and it was held that this kind of omnibus evidence naturally has to be very carefully scruinised in order to eliminate all chances of false or mistaken identification. 

 18. In the case of Seraj Din Vs Kala and another, (1964) 16 D. L. R. (SC)-94 Test Identification parade of the accused whom the witnesses saw for a short time has been stressed. It has been held that in such a case in the absence of T. I. parade the evidence of the witnesses identifying the accused in Court should not be given any importance. 

 In the case of State Vs. Abdul. Rahman & Hakim (1975) 27 DLR 77 it was held: 

 "It is very difficult for the witnesses to identify the accused standing in dock but such identification should not be given, any importance particularly in a case where the test identification parade should have been held, but it has not been held and the witnesses had been given an opportunity to see the accused, before the trial." 

 19. We respectfully agree with the views expressed in the aforesaid decisions. In the instance case 5 witnesses have identified the appellants in dock without mentioning their names. There is no evidence that those witnesses had previous acquaintances with these appellants who were men of different villages and of different police stations. The occurrence in the houses of these P.Ws. took place at about midnight The means of recognition are said to be the focuses of the torch-lights of the miscreants and in case of P. W.2 a hurricane is said to have been burning in his hut, The witnesses were not put to any test identification parade although it is a case where the witnesses ought to have been put on test identification parade. Following the guideline laid down in the aforesaid case we are of the opinion that only an omnibus statement that all the appellants participated in the offences and the identification of all of them in general in dock during the trial, in the absence of any lest identification parade itself cannot establish the guilt of the appellants. In the circumstances, chances of false or mistaken identification cannot be ruled out. We are, therefore, of the opinion that the appellants of this category are entitled to benefit of doubt. 

 20. Thus, on an analysis of the entire evidence and the facts and circumstances of the case we find that the guilt of appellants Abdul Majid, Abdur Rahim alias Jinnah, Malequl Islam, Jafar Ali and Azizul Islam have been All established. We think they have been rightly convicted and sentenced by the learned Magistrate and we uphold the same. 

 21. The guilt of the appellants Sadequl Islam alias Sedeque Ali, Shamsuddin, Abdur Razzaque, Osman Ali Mondal, Mozahar alias Mozahar Ali, Kazi Ansarul Islam, Alam Mia, Muzaffar Hossain alias Choin, Mosiruddin Akond, Asiruddin Mondal, Abdul Latif, Jahurul Islam, Matiar Rahman, Parjoar Pahan and Jerku Pahan have not been established and we set aside their conviction and sentence and acquit them. It is directed that they be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
